entries.subject: LAM/SPHERE MPCD: selected reconstruction
entries.finding: The current LAM 3Dshape directory lists 2_Pallas_mpcd.obj, matching the actual preparation input. The retained measurements describe 22530 vertices and 45056 facets in km; the recipe preserves that source scale. This review checked the release listing and local source/recipe binding, not a fresh mesh reconstruction or new source-fit test.

entries.subject: Size and pole
entries.finding: The retained Table 1 and Table A.1 extract records diameter 511 km, ecliptic J2000 pole (42°, -15°), period 7.81321 h. Published survey diameter averages ADAM and MPCD; the released MPCD coordinates are not rescaled to that average. The measured source volume-equivalent radius is 254.07824138806413 km. These source interpretations were checked against the recipe; the paper table was not freshly re-transcribed in this pass.

entries.subject: Released SPHERE observations and surface registration
entries.finding: Final bounded joint registration of the 05:04, 05:08 and 06:05 Camera 2 images used lit outlines and interior matches with the released MPCD mesh and spin fixed. The previously examined 06:05 holdout remains at 2.610 pixels RMS, maximum 5.460. That camera solution was frozen before checking the unused 06:07:17 Camera 2 photograph; with limb-only pointing and no interior adjustment, eight held-out matches give 5.289 pixels RMS, maximum 8.178. All fourteen matches in that fresh frame were evaluation data. This attempt is closed without a photographic surface. It does not prove registration impossible. Earlier simultaneous-camera, short/long transfer, image-identity and source-orientation evidence remains retained; the new evidence adds eight verified input pins and 51 recast/replayed control residuals.
entries.revisitWhen: New producer-controlled image geometry or independently verified surface correspondences with measured localization precision would reopen photographic preparation. Joint image-and-limb fitting has now been tried and failed the frozen fresh-exposure check; do not restart equivalent fits to the same uncertain controls. The inherited one-pixel criterion, telescope PSF and raster pole arrows are not established SPHERE camera-error bounds.

entries.subject: Released ADAM companion model
entries.finding: The live directory also lists 2_Pallas_adam.obj. The body’s retained model comparison already distinguishes this ADAM reconstruction from the selected MPCD mesh. It is not adopted as a duplicate view of the same measured shape; the original comparison remains linked. Revisited for the photographic frame investigation: DAMIT model 4395, explicitly linked to Marsset et al. (2020), supplies a shape table and separate IAUspin record. Its 1602 vertices and 3200 indexed triangles match the LAM ADAM file exactly apart from a constant translation of (0.066526, 0.043641, 0.075851) km. Maximum residual after that translation is below 5e-14 km. A different ADAM geometry therefore does not explain the unqualified crater-to-image correspondence. It remains excluded as a duplicate delivered shape view; the published model and frame remain useful registration evidence.
entries.revisitWhen: An observation or scientific comparison specifically requires this alternative mesh and its matching source frame.

entries.subject: Marsset 2020 Figure 3 as a photographic map
entries.finding: Read the full article and 40-page supplement. Figure 3 is a Mollweide map of crater annotations, not a photographic raster, so it cannot supply a surface texture. The separately investigated crater-control route remains unresolved.
entries.revisitWhen: A separately released photographic raster, with map coordinates and reuse terms, would reopen the map-as-texture route.

entries.subject: Published crater coordinates as image registration controls
entries.finding: Four tentative native centres were recorded before projecting published coordinates with frozen ADAM and MPCD cameras. Toxa, Xyston and Akontia differ by 23–29 pixels; Hoplon by 9–11 pixels. The identification regions are not confidence intervals, so those discrepancies do not establish camera error or model incompatibility. Quadratic illumination correction did not resolve the identities, and no rigid-frame correction was adopted. The shared checker replays input pins, projections, visibility and residuals; its five focused tests and the preparation TypeScript project passed. The later ten-image sequence confirms a persistent lower-right structure, but does not establish its named-crater coordinates. See surface-imagery for the newly identified published-photo pairing. Earlier trials remain in the pinned evidence.
entries.revisitWhen: Use the identified 05:08:49 Camera 2 / Vernazza Figure B.2 pairing to resolve the remaining image-to-model pose and interior correspondence. Explain the published pole-marker discrepancy before adopting a correction. Revisit named controls only with new identification or coordinate-frame evidence; do not repeat fits to the same tentative picks.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with the cross-frame registration test on 55 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1), each held against a reference built from the body's frames more than an hour away, cast through the ADAM reconstruction with the survey's rotation record read longitude-first. Disc interior 9169 pixels (median); peak correlation 0.12 (median) against a mirror margin of 0.52; 0 of 55 frames decisive by the stated rule (peak at least 0.15 and margin at least 1.5), of which 0 peak within 5 degrees of the model. The frames carry no markings the test can register, so nothing in them confirms or refutes the rotation record's phase, pole or handedness; the silhouette gate that qualified Kleopatra cannot judge a body this round either. A photograph lens for this body would rest on the survey's record read by the route proven on Vesta and on five elongated bodies, with no check on this body itself; it is not derived until one exists.
entries.revisitWhen: A registration reference for this body: a spacecraft map, or frames in which the cross-frame test resolves markings (peak correlation above 0.15 with a mirror margin above 1.5 on most frames).
